title: PDSCEA: A phylo-developmental atlas of auditory-vocal circuit evolution and speech lateralization
research_question: How did evolution repurpose ancient primate auditory-vocal circuits into a developmentally organized and partly left-lateralized human speech network?
primary_hypothesis: An integrated model of conserved communication-signal representations, human auditory-motor connectivity, developmental lateralization, and speech-specific temporal coupling will explain learned vocal control better than single-region, FOXP2-only, or left-hemisphere-only models.

cohorts.nonhuman_primate: existing approved datasets preferred; new collection only after species-specific review
cohorts.design_note: Targets are planning parameters, not completed enrollment or observed sample sizes.

tasks: pure-tone and spectrally rotated speech controls
measurements: family structure or genotype when consent permits

equations.hierarchical_model: Y_idt = beta0 + beta1 Species_i + beta2 Age_i + beta3 Hemisphere_d + beta4 Task_t + beta5 Connectivity_id + beta6 Species_i*Age_i + beta7 Task_t*Connectivity_id + u_site + u_i + epsilon_idt
equations.mediation: M_i = a0 + a1 Age_i + a2 Species_i + a3 Family_i + u_i + e_i; Y_i = c0' + c1' Age_i + c2' Species_i + c3' M_i + c4' Handedness_i + v_i + eta_i

controls: motion, hearing status, site, age, sex, handedness, and language background covariates
falsification_rules: cross-species alignment does not exceed matched non-vocal controls
auditory-motor connectivity adds no held-out predictive value
developmental lateralization trajectory is absent or fully explained by handedness
speech-specific dynamic coupling disappears after controls
single-region or FOXP2-only model performs as well or better under the prespecified complexity penalty
ethics: informed consent, guardian consent, and child assent
institutional review and privacy-preserving data governance
prefer reuse of approved primate data and apply species-specific welfare review
